title: First dates, Emerette and Sundays at the Robin Hood
summary: No dating before service; after discharge he went out with Emerette, Marino and Moran, hearing Paul Gayten and trying to sing.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: I guess we can back up. Do you remember your first date, the girl? Do you remember your first date? You were calling somebody on the phone? Or whatever? No, no telephone. No, no telephone. Telephone. So you didn't, so your house, when you were
growing up, you didn't have a phone? No, not at all. And my first date, my first date had to be, you know, would have memory, not before I went into service, had to be after.
So you don't remember dating before you went into service? No. I mean going out with your

own place? No, no. No, not at all. You see, you know, back then it's altogether different from what it is now. You know, like, you talking about virgin boys? Virgin? Yeah. Strictly. So who was the first girl that you met? Well, what I can remember, the first girl I met, Mabel was Emma Rett. When I came out of the service, that was the first girl I met. And she wanted to be my girlfriend. And we did, we'd go out, me, Emma Rett, Marino with Harriet, and Moran with Gloria Bell. So we, the three of us were buddies, and we would always go out together on Sundays. Always was Sundays. Where would y'all go? We would catch the bus and go in town. We used to go to Robin Hood. Well, that was, see, that was before my singing. We was, I mean, we all, Moran was the drummer, Larry Marino was the saxophone player. And I was a singer. So we, we all went to Greenwald Music School together. And so we all, our, our girlfriends were friends. So we used to go to Robin Hood. We used to go around and hear Paul Gaten. And that's when I'd go there every Sunday, always trying to get on the bandstand and sing, and Sporty Johnson would never let me sing. Never would let me sing. And I, well, I was an amateur, you know, but I tried, and not, and nothing didn't happen until Doudrop, when I won that amateur contest, you know. So.
So, let, let, we can, um, so the girl you, the girl you went out with on this one time?

With Amaret. Yeah, well, we went out quite a bit. Yeah. We went out quite a bit. Yeah. Quite a bit. Every Sunday. In fact, her mama thought I was going to marry her. Mm-hmm. I guess. Because, uh, I bought a ring. It was a birthstone ring. For her? Yeah. And I think her mama was under the impression that it was an engagement ring. But her mama said, well, yeah, ain't nobody getting married, because Amaretta's going to school. Mm-hmm. And so, Amaretta did wind up, Amaretta wind up at Southern University of Baton Rouge, but then I met my wife. Uh-huh. And, uh, we wind up married, and Amaretta was in college, and that was the end of that, and the next thing I know, she was married to Venice Beldman.
